sections.h2: Fast sale options in North Tonawanda
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a direct cash purchase, and the choice usually turns on the condition of the house and how long you can wait. Start by confirming your address is inside the city, because the 14120 ZIP code also covers southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton.

North Tonawanda is a city in Niagara County, bounded by the Niagara River on the west and Tonawanda Creek and the Erie Canal on the south. Population is 29,806, down 2.3% from 2020. It is the second-largest city in the county after Niagara Falls.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $197,200
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.1%
  • Median gross rent: $934 a month
  • Median household income: $66,961

With 14,015 households averaging 2.14 people, the city skews toward long-time owners. About 91% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to a settled owner base.

sections.h2: Homes built in the Lumber City
sections.html:
The city calls itself the Lumber City, and its housing grew out of that history. From the mid-19th century into the 1970s it was a lumber forwarding center, and more than 150 lumber companies operated here. The Ray H. Bennett Lumber Company sold kit homes across the United States and Canada for about 70 years, so you may own a kit house without knowing it. Goundry Street has mansions built for lumber barons.

Downtown draws buyers who like the Riviera Theatre on Webster Street, the City Market, Gateway Harbor Park on the canal, and Gratwick-Riverside Park, a 53-acre park on the Niagara River.

Under Chapter 51D of the city code, every owner of rental property in North Tonawanda registers each rental unit with the Building Department, and owner-occupied properties register too, without a fee.

PropertyFee
1 to 3 dwelling units$35 per unit
4 or more dwelling units$140
Owner-occupiedNo fee, registration still required

A certificate is valid up to one year or until ownership changes, so the buyer of a rental house registers in their own name after the deed transfers. Registering consents to inspection by Code Enforcement for compliance with the city chapter and the New York State building and fire codes.

  • Applicants submit photo identification.
  • An owner who does not live in Niagara County, Erie, Genesee or Orleans County must name a property manager who does, and who can accept legal notices.
  • A first conviction for failing to register carries a fine of $250 to $500. A second within twelve months carries $500 to $2,500.
  • A fine unpaid after 30 days becomes a lien on the property and is collected like a tax.

If you own a rental, clear any registration gap before you sell, since a lien would surface in a title search. The Building Department is at 216 Payne Avenue, and its number is (716) 692-2680.

Grievance Day is always the fourth Tuesday in May, and the Assessor's office has the forms starting in March. The Assessor's online property search lets you open any parcel and select Additional Info, then View Tax Detail, to see a tax summary by year.

Buyers often ask about exemptions, so know the basics:

  • Basic STAR requires owning and living in the home with income of $500,000 or less.
  • Enhanced STAR requires age 65 and adjusted gross income of $110,750 or less.
  • People who bought after 2015 sign up with the state for the STAR Credit.
  • The low-income senior exemption has an income limit of $34,400, and the disability exemption has a limit of $34,600.
  • Military service exemptions are capped for assessments above $120,000.

The Assessor will give you a free copy of your deed on request, which helps when you are assembling closing papers. Call 695-8597 for details.

sections.h2: Deeds, transfer tax and city water
sections.html:
Deeds for a North Tonawanda sale go to the Niagara County Clerk, not City Hall. The clerk's deed recording office is at (716) 439-7022, with recording hours of 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays.

The clerk requires the signed original deed plus a TP-584 transfer tax return and an RP-5217 real property transfer report. The seller pays the state transfer tax of $2 for each $500, or $4 per $1,000, due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. A closing attorney or title company normally handles this for you.

Before closing, settle city water. After two consecutive estimated water meter readings, a $25 fee applies each quarter until the meter is read, and readings can be dropped off or submitted online. Ask the Treasurer's office at (716) 695-8575 for the current balance and how it is handled at transfer.

The North Tonawanda City School District serves the city, with a high school, a middle school, an intermediate school and three elementary schools. The mean commute is 20.4 minutes. Precipitation falls on about 171 days a year and snow on about 57, so roof, gutter and basement condition deserve a close look before you list.

Gather your deed, recent tax and water statements, and a payoff letter. If the house is a rental, confirm the registration with the Building Department first. Ask your attorney which forms your sale needs, and ask the Assessor for the free deed copy. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, which spares you showings and repair credits, and closing follows your own calendar once the title work is done.

Ask the Treasurer for the water balance a few days before closing so no surprise reaches the table. At the closing you sign the deed and the transfer tax forms, the mortgage is paid, and the clerk records the deed. If you were a landlord, remember that the buyer registers the units in their own name afterward.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in North Tonawanda if it is not registered?
faqs.a: Register it before the sale. Failing to register is a violation with fines of $250 to $500 for a first conviction, and an unpaid fine becomes a lien on the property.

faqs.q: Where do I file a deed after selling in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: File it with the Niagara County Clerk. The seller pays transfer tax of $2 per $500, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms go in with the deed.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: It is always the fourth Tuesday in May. Grievance forms are available from the Assessor's office starting in March.

faqs.q: Is a 14120 mailing address always inside North Tonawanda city limits?
faqs.a: No. The ZIP code 14120 also covers southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton, so check your tax bill to see which municipality governs your house.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The certificate lasts up to one year or until ownership changes. After the sale the new owner registers the units with the Building Department.
